findings.verdict: HAVC earns a place in our pipeline. Its repaired assisted result is good and close to the curated baseline. The tested automatic recipe still needs help on wide shots, so it does not yet replace curation.
findings: The earlier paired-only test undersold HAVC. Single-image generation, iterative Fix Colors and RGB-preserving Fix Image repairs keep the purple costume through all six shot intervals. I still prefer the curated FLUX baseline’s blue sky and costume contrast, but assisted HAVC is a credible alternative.

Movie-only automation produces a mostly coherent gold palette. One unchanged global palette prompt makes the medium shot and long close-up purple without per-reference work, then loses it in the wide shot and much of the return shot. Manually verified resets alone recover return and feet colors but leave the wide shot weak.

Reuse of one corrected wide reference restores purple through motion. Raising propagation from 640 to 1920, proximity bias, smaller memory windows, and prompt rewriting did not fix the tested weak correspondences. Build automatic reference validation and reuse around these existing tools; keep CMNET2.

findings.watch_for: Watch 109–115 s for the wide shot, 115–118.6 s for the return, and 118.6–119.76 s for the feet. The assisted version preserves costume color through all of them. Source dissolves remain visible; they are not generated motion.
findings.automatic_recipe: The final movie-only run froze 15 anchors before continuous GUI-style propagation, with a 15-reference window, slide step one, 640-pixel width, no cut resets, no proximity bias, and no retry. A complete 1920-pixel run and three 100-frame memory controls informed the selection. Final raw predictions exactly match the earlier 640 run across all 750 frames.
findings.palette_automatic_recipe: The one-palette control uses the same automatically selected BW frames and one identical palette prompt for every anchor, fixed before execution. It has no reference review or correction. Its optional reset-only control uses our manually verified cut manifest, so it is assisted. Those resets improve return and feet but do not fully recover the wide shot. Matched 25-frame reset controls at 640 and 1920 show no benefit from higher resolution.
findings.assisted_recipe: Seventeen single-image anchors received explicit costume roles. I rejected five for invented composition or wrong role colors. Fix Colors transferred accepted colors to original BW geometry; Fix Image preserved RGB during narrow edits. One chosen wide palette was reused at three times, and an explicit foreground/right male instruction corrected the return shot. Final propagation uses shot-local banks and manually verified boundaries. Matched 640/960/1920 close and wide controls showed no clear quality gain from more pixels.
findings.repair_caption: Four actual motion samples at source frames 2786, 2791, 2796 and 2810. Independently repaired references still weaken purple with all-bank, shot-only or proximity-biased propagation. Reusing one chosen wide palette improves purple and garden color.
findings.cost_scope: Movie-only generation 880.19 s plus final propagation/delivery 150.93 s; one-palette generation 884.67 s plus 151.50 s. Extraction and dedup are additional. Assisted recorded work totals 1900.85 s and charges the entire six-image development batch that supplied one reused wide candidate, as well as 17 initial anchors, six repair candidates, transfers and final render. Other development controls and discarded attempts are separate. The full investigation recorded 2.56 hours of guarded jobs, plus one interrupted rewriting trial without a final guard record. Active agent/human minutes were not measured. Baseline accepted generation was 92 s for nine in-interval anchors, while propagation used all 87 anchors over 180 s; revision/search costs are incomplete.
findings.validation: Each final HAVC delivery decodes 750 frames at 25 fps, 30 s of video and audio, 1920×1080, and under the 16,867,622-byte cap. I inspected all 750 consecutive decoded frames for each primary case and five cut neighborhoods. Source-flow chroma and luma checks supplement that review; they are not perceptual quality scores. Mypy, Ruff and all 70 tests passed. Coloring and GPU tests ran serially in tmux under the memory guard. The smallest recorded system headroom across guarded development jobs was 159.3 GiB. An initial full-resolution low-cap MPS allocation failed cleanly; the bounded larger-cap rerun completed.
findings.parity: A fresh native MPS single-image run reproduces the same enlarged-figure/composition problem as MLX on the difficult wide anchor. Its pixel MAE against MLX is 5.897/255, so it is not exact parity. Earlier paired checks were closer. The exact text-weight cache passes a separate byte-identical PNG check. CPU FP32 VAE is required on this machine to avoid numerical corruption.

findings.draft_reply:
Thanks for pointing me to HAVCServerDiT. I installed it through a Mac adapter and reran the same 30-second clip with Fast Pipeline disabled, native six-step Qwen2.1/Viggle, updated reference deduplication, and your Fix Colors/Fix Image workflow. Reusing and repairing references gives a good assisted result; my first paired-only comparison missed that.

With one unchanged palette prompt, close-ups hold the requested purple, but the distant wide shot fades toward beige. Higher-resolution propagation did not recover it in matched tests. Manually verified interval resets improve the return and feet shots; reusing a corrected wide reference fixes the wide shot. The report includes complete aligned videos and the Mac-specific limits.

The distinction I meant was feeding earlier accepted colored examples into generation of a new reference. At the pinned revision, I see current BW plus text entering DiT, paired inputs converted to BW, and colored-reference memory entering CMNET2 afterward. The optional retry can add a new BW-generated anchor, and the assisted tools already provide useful reuse operations. Am I missing a configured path that passes earlier colored exemplars into the automatic DiT request? That is the part I want to automate.

I would keep CMNET2 and build reference validation and reuse around these tools. This test does not justify a general judgment against FLUX: our curated FLUX baseline still has the look I prefer on this clip, but its curation cost is not matched to these runs.
